“HH model is the most accurate and computationally inexpensive SN model; LIF and Izhikevish models are the most expensive, and inaccurate; HHT model is less accurate and more expensive than HH model due the table discretization; HHT model should not be compared to IZH model; the number of dimensions is not an accurate indicator of the computational cost of SNs; and the search of an optimal simulation is problem-specific”.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SNs are more efficient than what was thought before, and the HH model, without using tables, is the most efficient SN.
the computational cost is not a good indicator of the simulation accuracy and that the accuracy is the best indicator of the computational cost.
the SNs are not comparable in computational capacities and accuracy, and the simulation of a given SN is a problem-specific multiobjective optimization problem with no unique solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the computational cost is a function of the SN model accuracy, the SN discontinuity, the SN input current, and the SN simulation parameters.
the SN simulation is a multiobjective problem and that the simulation parameters are problem-dependent.
the SN simulation is not a trivial task, and that the choice of the SN implementation should be carefully made.
